削 concerns shaving or cutting material away. 削る けずる can mean sharpening a pencil by shaving it, reducing an amount, or deleting part of a text. In 削除 さくじょ, the focus is deletion or erasure, not necessarily a physical cut.

Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology: Picture the 肖-shaped left part as a block with small marks above it, being shaved by the blade radical 刂 on the right. This invented scene is a memory aid, not a historical explanation or a verified phonetic analysis.
サク
削除 さくじょ — deletion; erasure
けず.る
削る けずる — shave; sharpen; pare; cut down
はつ.る
削る はつる — shave off, especially concrete; usually written はつる; also written 斫る in construction
そ.ぐ
削ぐ そぐ — chip, shave or slice off

This card selects サク and けず.る for reading questions. The other two readings remain useful recognition information, not invalid or obsolete pronunciations. The dots mark the written ending: 削る has る outside the kanji, while 削ぐ has ぐ.
削る けずる — shave; sharpen; cut down
削除 さくじょ — deletion; erasure
削減 さくげん — reduction; cut
添削 てんさく — correction of writing
Two practical uses of けずる are 鉛筆を削る (えんぴつをけずる), "sharpen a pencil," and 予算を削る (よさんをけずる), "cut the budget."

The indexing radical is 刀; its visible form here is 刂. 消 also has a 肖-shaped part, but its left side is 氵 rather than the right-side 刂 of 削. Erasing and deleting meanings can overlap; these shapes do not create an absolute semantic boundary.
The spelling 削る can represent the separate verb はつる as well as けずる. The linked word article teaches けずる. JMdict's "take a percentage" sense belongs to its separate はつる entry, not the けずる lesson.
削ぐ そぐ is another verb, not a different spelling of けずる. It also has figurative weakening or dampening uses; JMdict marks those senses as usually written in kana, not every physical use of 削ぐ.
Compare the right-side 刂 in 前, 判 and 刑. Their meanings are not shaving or sharpening; a shared radical does not make the words interchangeable.

Metadata: KANJIDIC2, 2026-11-02 snapshot. Word families: JMdict, entries 1298040, 1298090, 1298100, 1298110, 1298120, 1440850 and 1915010. Reading allocation and usage: Digital Daijisen, 削, 削る and 削除.
削る けずる — shave; sharpen; cut down
削る means shaving or scraping material away, including sharpening a pencil. It also means cutting down an amount, such as a budget, expenses, or time. This is a transitive godan verb: 削ります, 削って, 削らない.
ナイフで鉛筆を削ります。 (ナイフでえんぴつをけずります。) - I sharpen a pencil with a knife.
予算を削りました。 (よさんをけずりました。) - We cut the budget.
A further use is deleting or striking out part of a text: 不要な一文を削りました。 (ふようないちぶんをけずりました。) - I deleted an unnecessary sentence. This deletion use is additional teaching, not a separate N2 assignment.
削 contributes cutting away or shaving. The native reading is けず.る: the kanji supplies けず, and る is the written ending. This is one native verb, not a combination of on readings.
減らす (へらす) more generally means reducing an amount. 省く (はぶく) overlaps in omission or cutting down; 消す (けす) overlaps in erasing. 切る (きる) has broader cutting uses, including reductions.

削る need not mean removing a large piece in one cut; shaving a surface is a central use. Nor does every use require repeated tiny reductions. The source list's "take a percentage" belongs to the separate reading はつる in JMdict, not this けずる entry. Do not learn it here as a general expression for charging commission.
Dictionary: JMdict, entry 1298090, selected senses 1-2 and additional sense 3; separate はつる entry 1298100, sense 2. Usage check: Daijisen, hosted by Weblio, separate けずる, はつる, and へずる entries.
削 contributes cutting away or shaving. The native reading is けず.る: the kanji supplies けず, and る is the written ending. This is one native verb, not a combination of on readings.
削除 さくじょ — deletion; erasure
削除 is deletion or elimination, especially removing writing, entries, or data. 削除する is transitive: the item removed takes を.
重複した行を削除しました。 (ちょうふくしたぎょうをさくじょしました。) - I deleted the duplicate line.
このファイルを削除してもいいですか。 (このファイルをさくじょしてもいいですか。) - May I delete this file?
削除されたファイル (さくじょされたファイル) is "a deleted file"; された is passive.

削 contributes shaving or cutting away, and 除 contributes removal or exclusion. The related meanings reinforce taking something out. The on readings are サク + ジョ, with a small ょ. Deleting a line is not a claim that paper was physically shaved.
消す (けす) also covers erasing or deleting, as well as turning off lights. 除く (のぞく) is broader removal or exclusion. 追加 (ついか), "addition," supplies a practical contrast when editing a list.

The legacy source's "cancellation" should not make 削除する a general verb for canceling an event. 中止 (ちゅうし) concerns calling off or discontinuing an activity. Deleting a calendar entry and canceling the event itself are different actions. The word alone also does not promise that deleted data can be recovered.

除 concerns taking something away or leaving it out. 除く のぞく can describe physical removal, but also an exception: 日曜日を除く (にちようびをのぞく), "excluding Sundays."
Modern-shape mnemonic: imagine clearing the 余-shaped piece away from the left-hand 阝. This is a visual reminder of removal, not an etymology.

掃除 uses ジ, not ジョ; learn its whole reading そうじ. Excluding a day from a schedule does not remove that day from the calendar: the scope of the statement changes. 降 shares left-hand 阝 but not the 余 on its right.
